newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Mir's solar alignment system malfunctions.
newsitem.headline: Mir's solar alignment system malfunctions.

text.p: The navigation devices that should keep the solar energy panels of Russia's Mir space station lined up on the Sun are malfunctioning, deputy mission chief Sergei Krikalyov told Reuters on Thursday.

"Mir is on its set orbit, but we're having to fire the engines more often. All the gyrodines are malfunctioning," he said, adding that there was no danger for the Russian-American crew. Mir lost up to half its electric power in an accident last week. Without gyrodines to keep the solar panels lined up on the Sun, the station needs to burn up fuel to keep its alignment.

Since colliding last week with an unmanned cargo craft that punctured one of Mir's modules and cut off power from some solar panels, the two Russians and one American on board have struggled to maximise electric power from the remaining panels.

Krikalyov said the reason for the gyrodine malfunction was not known. The ageing station has been in a vicious circle in which the loss of electric power has made it harder to power the gyrodines and keep the station in line with the Sun. That in turn had further reduced power. Mir can use its rocket engines to adjust its alignment, but fuel supplies are limited.
Krikalyov said there was enough fuel to adjust the alignment of the station. A cargo craft is due to blast off on Saturday carrying supplies to repair the damaged electric power system.

The voices of the crew -- commander Vasily Tsibliyev, flight engineer Alexander Lazutkin and NASA physicist Michael Foale -- sounded calm during radio conversations on Thursday with Mission Control near Moscow, which were monitored by journalists.
